q: What is the unit of energy, and how many joules are there in one kilojoule?
a: The unit of energy is the joule (J). One kilojoule is $1000\,\text{J}$.

q: Convert $3.2\,\text{MJ}$ to kilojoules using the value of the prefix.
A torch battery gives out $12\,\text{kJ}$, of which $3\,\text{kJ}$ turns into light. What does the remaining $9\,\text{kJ}$ turn into, and why has no energy been lost?
a: The remaining $9\,\text{kJ}$ turns into heat. No energy has been lost, because the energy of the light and the heat together is $3\,\text{kJ} + 9\,\text{kJ} = 12\,\text{kJ}$, which is the same as at the start.
